subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw support preserving and resuming an interrupted turn after injecting new user input, beyond its current boundary-steering and abort-and-replace contracts?
rationale: Current main intentionally separates safe same-turn boundary injection from cancellation and replacement; combining them creates a new cross-runtime transcript, tool, and provider lifecycle that cannot be selected mechanically.

options.title: Design resumable soft steer
options.body: Specify provider-neutral partial-output, tool-state, capability, continuation, and fallback semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep current contracts
options.body: Retain boundary steering plus abort-and-replace and explicitly document that an interrupted generation is not resumed.

options.title: Limit to native runtimes
options.body: Offer resumable behavior only for harnesses that expose a proven native interrupted-turn continuation protocol.

recommendation.title: Design resumable soft steer
recommendation.body: Specify provider-neutral partial-output, tool-state, capability, continuation, and fallback semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current product boundary, queue-steering history, and existing issue review make steipete the strongest available owner for this lifecycle decision.
